preprocessing: sharp/canvas: greyscale → resize to width 1200 → [preprocess.js] contrast stretch (1st–99th percentile) → Otsu threshold → display panel = largest light 4-connected region not touching the photo border and ≥4% of the area (fallback: whole photo) → crop to its bounding box → re-stretch + Otsu inside the crop → paint dark regions connected to the crop border white → two variants: A = stretched greyscale, B = Otsu black/white → resize to width 700 → pad 40px white
rule: Each variant is parsed by core/ocr.js parseHbDisplay. Accept only if (a) both variants return status "candidate" with the same value (unit kept only if both read the same unit; one unit missing → unit null, worker selects; two different units → reject), or (b) exactly one variant returns "candidate" and the other returns "no_reading" (no plausible number, no decimal-less number) or "low_confidence" whose plausible numbers all equal the candidate value; unit then kept only if the other variant read no unit or the same unit. Anything else — different values, ambiguous/decimal_suspect/unit_conflict in either variant beside a candidate, or no candidate at all — is rejected and the worker types the reading.
